weeks.title: Baseline and lab setup: database baseline assessment (TECHNICAL_GROWTH.md Section 11); MySQL 8.4 in Docker with performance_schema and sys schema enabled; a data generator for 5–10M rows; a repeatable way to measure query latency and insert throughput. Topic: InnoDB pages, B+ tree structure, clustered index.

Reads: secondary index lookups and the extra clustered-index lookup, composite indexes and leftmost prefix, covering indexes, range conditions, cardinality and histograms, EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

Writes: index maintenance on insert/update/delete, page splits, change buffer, sequential vs random primary keys (auto-increment vs UUIDv4 vs UUIDv7), measuring insert throughput and storage with 0, 2, 5, and 8 secondary indexes.

Transactions: MVCC and read views, isolation levels with REPEATABLE READ as default, consistent vs locking reads, record/gap/next-key locks, reproducing a lost update and a deadlock by hand. Monthly checkpoint.

deliverables.text: Reproducible SQL experiments (scripts committed, with predictions written before running).
Query-plan comparisons.
An index-design case study based on a real slow query from my job (anonymized).
A technical note explaining the observed behavior and production implications.

exit.text: given an unseen table, workload, and query, I can predict the plan and the cost of adding an index, then confirm or explain the discrepancy with measurements (Track A index topics at Level 3).

deliverables.text: A lab service implementing one domain with explicit invariants, structured into controller/service/repository with deliberate module boundaries.
An explicit business-rule and API specification for it, naming where each invariant is enforced.
Automated tests covering success, failure, and boundary cases, running against a real MySQL instance in CI.
A written review of one real module at work: where its business rules live, which boundaries leak, and what I would change.

exit.text: I can explain where each business rule is enforced and why, and my tests catch a deliberately introduced invariant violation.

deliverables.text: A background processing workflow.
Automated tests for duplicate processing and retry behavior.
A documented failure-recovery strategy.
A reproducible concurrency experiment (concurrent balance updates with at least two concurrency-control strategies compared).

exit.text: the import stays correct when the same file is uploaded twice, when a worker is killed mid-run, and when the same transaction arrives concurrently — demonstrated by tests, not by argument.

deliverables.text: A deployable application (multi-stage Docker image, non-root, CI pipeline).
Health checks and useful operational telemetry (structured logs with correlation IDs, RED metrics, traces).
A reproducible performance test with a profiled bottleneck and a measured fix.
An incident simulation (for example, a slow dependency causing cascading failure) and a blameless root-cause analysis.

exit.text: given a performance or reliability symptom I have not seen before, I can locate the cause with tools and explain it, rather than guess.

deliverables.text: A system design document for a real system from my job, taken at 100× its current load.
At least two alternative designs with explicit trade-offs.
An architecture decision record.
A design review conducted as a Senior Engineer would conduct it.
Weekly timed design exercises (45 minutes each, at least four in the month).

exit.text: in a timed exercise on an unseen problem, I produce estimates, a design, and trade-offs that hold up to follow-up questions.

deliverables.text: A completed, demonstrable backend capability, owned end to end (default: the Month 3 import pipeline extended to be resumable, observable, and load-tested). A feature I own at work counts, if I can publish an anonymized account of it.
A concise architecture document.
Automated test evidence and operational documentation.
A retrospective covering mistakes, trade-offs, and improvements.
Interview preparation: two mock system design interviews, a bank of deep technical questions drawn from my own notes, and five STAR stories from real work.
A final competency assessment against the initial baseline.

unplanned.work: B+tree index internals (structure, split, slotted page, buffer pool, covering index, heap/MVCC) — conceptual only, no measurements; PostgreSQL-shaped, see open question 1

items.text: Level 3 in Track A (database), transactions/concurrency, and idempotent async processing.
Level 3 in at least two of: observability, performance diagnosis, system design.
Level 2 minimum in every other area of the baseline table, with no area left at Level 0.
Level 4 in at least one topic, demonstrated on a real problem from my job.

Covering index / Index Only Scan and its cost
TOAST and the real cost of SELECT *
